rules.body: Apply this guidance when deferred persistence belongs to a durable document buffer while the current view owns only its subscription. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Preserve that ownership distinction when introducing batching.

Route edits through the existing per-document trailing task. Restart its quiet interval on each edit, retain the latest text, and leave the task reusable after consumption. Evidence: TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst." TASK: "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/coordinator.js: "get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}" Keep the saved document identity bound to its buffer rather than consulting the current view when the timer fires.

Preserve persistence when an active document departs through navigation, close, or disposal: capture its buffer, detach its view subscription, and flush its pending edits before the departure returns. Do not cancel durable edits merely because the badge ends, or destroy the store-owned buffer. This preserves the original synchronous persistence behavior while delaying ordinary edits. Evidence: TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." src/coordinator.js: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}" README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge."

Treat persistence as a synchronous reentry boundary. Establish the departing-view state before flushing, and check that an outer navigation request is still authoritative after flushing before publishing its target. A save callback's newer navigation or close must not be overwritten by resumed outer work. Evidence: README.md: "Save callbacks can synchronously navigate." docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." src/coordinator.js: "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;"

Clear the consumed timer and pending value before invoking persistence, so synchronous callbacks cannot consume the same pending edit again and newly queued work survives the callback. Preserve the existing reusable flush semantics. Evidence: src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" The null sentinel must continue to permit valid empty text.

Preserve document rendering, matching-document status delivery, subscription cleanup, and public interfaces while changing edit scheduling. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." src/coordinator.js: "if(event.id===id)env.renderStatus(event);" docs/host-api.md: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()."

Keep transient preview policy separate from durable document persistence. Evidence: TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));\n  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};" Preserve its 40 ms interval, discard-on-hide behavior, and subsequent reuse.

Verify source-derived boundaries with controlled timers: no ordinary save before 120 ms of quiet; one latest-text save at the boundary; another successful burst; valid empty text; pending edits persisted before open, close, and dispose return; and synchronous save-listener navigation or close remaining authoritative. Check identity and subscription cleanup across departure and reopening. Separately verify unchanged preview timing, hide cancellation, and reuse. These checks operationalize TASK's "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." together with the quoted ownership, synchronous-listener, and trailing-task source semantics; evaluation results do not add requirements.

limitations: Applies where document buffers outlive view subscriptions, departure preserves edits, and persistence can synchronously invoke navigation.
Exception recovery, calls after disposal, and arbitration between concurrent workspaces are unspecified by the original task and supplied public sources.
Attempt 1 provides one successful implementation observation; it does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit across tasks.
Automatic Contract, AST hints, and evaluation observations are guidance only; the rules derive from TASK and the quoted public sources.
